content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in dense, data-driven utility apps for athletes — the kind of interface a lifter reads in a two-second glance between sets under gym lighting, never a marketing screen.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (dark, default):
- Canvas #0E1116, Card #161B22, Input surface #1F2630, Surface 3 (chips/thumbnails) #283040, Divider #262C36
- Action/brand (the single accent): #1E6FFF, pressed #1857CC, soft tint fill #14233F
- Text: primary #F2F4F8, secondary #9BA3B0, tertiary #5E6675
- Semantic: set-done green #2FBF71 (row wash at 16% alpha), PR gold #F5B83D (badge at 18% tint), destructive red #F1545B, warning amber #F5A623
- Optional light mode: canvas #F4F6FA, card #FFFFFF, input #EEF1F6, divider #E2E6EE

Typography: Inter throughout, tabular figures (tnum) mandatory on every numeric value. Ladder: screen title 32/800, section title 22/700, item title 18/700 (always in the accent blue), metric/timer 17/700 tabular, body 16/400, table-cell value 15/600 tabular, caption 13/500, uppercase column label 11/600 tracked +0.5, tab label 10/600, badge 10/800 uppercase.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit, scale 4-8-12-14-16-20-24-32-40-48-64. Card padding 14pt, card-to-card gap 14pt, set-row vertical padding 7pt (row height ~40pt), section gap 24pt. Radius scale: 8pt small cells, 10pt tonal controls, 12pt primary buttons/pills, 16pt cards, 20pt sheets, full pill for chips, circle for avatars/rings.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A five-column logging row: set-index chip, a 'last time' reference cell, two editable numeric cells, and a checkbox that washes the row green and fills solid on completion.
2. A countdown pill with a thin circular progress ring that sweeps as time elapses, offering a skip action and nudge controls.
3. A small tinted badge that appears the instant a logged number beats a stored best, with a spring pop and a single haptic pulse — never confetti.
4. Depth conveyed entirely by a surface-lightness ladder plus 1pt borders rather than drop shadows, reserving real shadows for sheets/overlays only.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never introduce a second accent hue — the one action color must carry every CTA, every active tab, and every entity-name heading in the app.
2. Every digit on screen — reps, weight, totals, timers — renders with tabular/monospaced figures; a layout that lets digits reflow is a defect, not a detail.
3. Always surface the prior value for whatever the user is about to re-enter, inline and dimmed, so they never have to leave the screen to know their target.
4. Completion states use a color wash plus an icon change together — never color alone — so the state reads even for a colorblind user glancing at speed.
5. Keep entry rows dense (sub-45pt height) deliberately; a workout logger should let a full routine fit on one screen mid-session, unlike a leisurely reading app.
6. Record-breaking or achievement moments get one small, quiet celebratory gesture (a badge pop + one haptic) — never a full-screen animation that interrupts the flow of logging.
7. Auto-advance the user into the next expected action (e.g., starting a rest countdown) the moment they complete a step, rather than waiting for a manual trigger.
8. Reserve real drop shadows for genuinely floating layers (sheets, pickers); flat cards on a dark canvas should use border + surface-step contrast instead, since shadows barely register on near-black.
9. Motion stays fast and functional (under ~300ms) everywhere except the countdown ring itself, which should tick continuously and predictably.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / brand accent color (hex):
- Core loggable entity (e.g., exercise set, task, drink, habit) and its 2-4 numeric fields:
- Primary session flow (what does an active 'session' look like, and how does the user finish it)?:
- Whether a 'previous value' reference should be shown per entry, and where it comes from:
- Celebration trigger (what counts as a 'record' worth flagging) and how it should be detected:
- Bottom navigation tabs (list 4-5, name the center/primary one if special):
- Light mode requirement (dark-only, dark-first with opt-in light, or both equal):
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version, or note if this should also inform Android/Web variants):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Swift `Color` and `Font` token extension file matching the palette and type ladder above, adapted to the project's stated accent color.
2. A SwiftUI view for the core logging row (index chip + reference value + editable numeric cell(s) + completion control), with the green-wash-on-complete behavior wired via state and animation.
3. A SwiftUI countdown/rest-timer pill component with a circular progress ring, skip button, and nudge controls.
4. A SwiftUI 'record' badge component with the spring-pop reveal and haptic trigger described in the house rules.
5. A card component for the primary repeating list unit (exercise/entry card) with header, body slot, and a footer 'add' affordance.
6. A bottom tab bar implementation matching the specified tabs, with the single-accent active-state treatment (no tint pill).
7. A short accessibility and Dynamic Type note: which text should scale, which must stay fixed (any digit-width-sensitive layout), and the VoiceOver phrasing for the logging row and the record badge.
</what_to_give_me>

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who builds clinical-but-warm health-tracking apps — interfaces that turn a day of data entry into a single glanceable progress gauge, without ever feeling cold or medical.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, default):
- Canvas #FFFFFF, Surface (row/card fill) #F5F7FA, Surface 2 (chips/inputs) #E5E9F0, Divider #E5E7EB
- Heritage brand blue #005DAA (used sparingly for legacy/branded moments), current action blue #0072CE (pressed #005FA8), tinted background #E7F0FF
- Fixed three-color macro trio, order never changes: macro-A orange #FF9F1C, macro-B purple #A463F2, macro-C green #19C37D
- Text: primary #1F2937, secondary #4B5563, tertiary #9CA3AF, hero-number ink #111827
- Semantic ring states: under-goal green #19C37D, on-track blue #0072CE, approaching-limit amber #F59E0B, over-limit red #EF4444
- Dark mode: canvas #0F1419, surface #1A1F26, divider #2A2F37, text primary #F3F4F6, action blue lifted to #3B8FDF for OLED legibility

Typography: system sans (SF Pro on iOS), tabular figures mandatory on every nutrition number. Ladder: hero ring number 56/700 tight tracking, large nav title 28/700, section header 22/700, sub-item title 18/600, list-item name 16/500, list-item value 16/600 tabular, macro number 22/700 tabular, uppercase macro/eyebrow label 11-13/600 tracked, button 16/600, tab label 10/600.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit up to 80pt. Standard horizontal margin 16pt (24pt on detail screens). List-row height ~64pt (intentionally dense for fast scanning). Radius scale: 12pt buttons/inputs, 16pt cards, 24pt bottom-sheet top corners, full pill for small status badges, circle for the floating action control.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A large circular ring gauge with a giant tabular number centered inside it, whose fill color changes meaning as a daily total accumulates (four distinct semantic states, not just a percentage).
2. A smaller three-slice ring breaking a total into fixed sub-categories, always in the same order and same three colors, with a legend row per slice.
3. Content organized into named, collapsible time-of-day or category sections, each with its own leading '+' quick-add affordance.
4. A circular floating action button centered above one specific tab (not a generic corner FAB), carrying a tinted shadow in the brand color rather than a neutral shadow.
5. A full-screen capture overlay (camera or scanner style) with corner-bracket framing and a pulsing scan-line guide.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Never let any numeral in a ring, chart, or ledger use proportional figures — tabular alignment is what makes a stacked list of totals readable at a glance.
2. The fixed sub-category color trio is sacred: never reorder it, never reuse those three hues anywhere else in the interface (not on a button, not on a tab, not as a status color).
3. The hero ring's fill color must flip semantically as the underlying value crosses defined thresholds (under target / on track / approaching / over) — a static single-color ring loses the app's core value proposition.
4. Keep the primary canvas clinically clean (pure white, hairline borders, near-zero shadow) and reserve the one meaningfully elevated shadow for the single floating action button, tinted with the brand color instead of neutral black.
5. Every repeating list row (food/entry row) should default to a dense height that favors fast scanning over generous whitespace — this is a ledger, and density is a feature, not a compromise.
6. Any milestone or streak counter gets a small celebratory flourish only at meaningful thresholds (e.g., 7/30/100-day marks) — never on every entry, or the celebration becomes noise.
7. Keep body and label text on a warm dark ink rather than pure black — the tone should read approachable, not sterile.
8. A premium/upsell accent color must never double as a primary action color — gating and doing are visually distinct languages.
9. Any modal capture flow (barcode/photo/etc.) should feel cinematic and full-screen, distinct from the rest of the clinical-white chrome.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / two-tone brand blue (heritage hex + current action hex):
- What the hero ring measures, and its 4 semantic threshold states:
- The fixed sub-category set for the secondary donut (name each, in order, with a color):
- How entries are organized (e.g., meal sections, time blocks, custom categories) and their fixed order:
- Quick-capture mechanism (barcode scan, photo, manual search) and where its FAB lives:
- Bottom navigation tabs (list 4-5):
- Whether there's a premium/gated tier and what its accent color should be:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version; note if Android/Web variants are also needed):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Swift `Color` and `Font` token extension file for light and dark mode, matching the palette/type ladder above adapted to the project's brand blue.
2. A SwiftUI hero-ring component with animated stroke fill, semantic color-state switching, and a centered tabular number with a smooth 'ticking' transition when the underlying value updates.
3. A SwiftUI secondary donut component for the fixed sub-category breakdown, with a legend row per slice.
4. A SwiftUI list-row component for a single ledger entry (name, subtitle/metadata, trailing tabular value, swipe-to-delete).
5. A collapsible section-header component grouping entries by category, with a leading quick-add row.
6. A circular floating action button positioned above a specific tab, with a brand-tinted shadow and a sheet it opens on tap.
7. Accessibility notes: VoiceOver phrasing for the hero ring and donut, and which elements should stay fixed-size under Dynamic Type versus scale freely.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in high-energy athletic broadcast-style interfaces — the visual register of a stadium jumbotron or a shoe-brand campaign, built for the adrenaline moment right before and during a hard workout.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Canvas: true black #000000 on every screen (no charcoal substitute), whisper-lighter section fill #0A0A0A, card surface #1A1A1A, pressed/input surface #2B2B2B, hairline divider #333333
- The one radioactive accent (progress rings, active states, primary CTAs when not white): #CCFF00, pressed #9FCC00
- The secondary intensity accent (results/celebration moments only): #FA5400, plus a sharper alert red #E50916 for max-effort/error states
- Text: white #FFFFFF primary, gray ladder #B3B3B3 / #8E8E8E / #5C5C5C for secondary/tertiary/quaternary
- Effort-zone gradient (5 bands, low to max): #3D87F4 blue, #48C77E green, #FFD600 yellow, #FA5400 orange, #E50916 red

Typography: a heavy condensed display face for every hero number and every button label (all set in full uppercase), paired with a standard system sans for body/metadata (mixed case allowed). Ladder: in-session hero stat 88/900 tight line-height (~0.95), pre/post-session hero 64/900, headline 48/900, section header 32/900 uppercase, sub-header 22/700 uppercase, stat label 13/700 uppercase with wide (+1.0pt) tracking, card title 17/700 (mixed case, system sans), body 15/400 system sans, button label 17/900 uppercase with +0.5pt tracking, tab label 10/600 mixed case.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit up to 80pt. Standard margin 16pt (24pt on the hero tracking screen). Radius scale: 8pt inputs, 16pt photo/quote cards, 32pt primary pill buttons (rounded but not a full capsule), full pill for small tags, circle for avatars and the large in-session action buttons.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A large circular progress ring in the radioactive accent, thick stroke, rounded cap, with a screaming hero number centered inside it during an active session — the single most recognizable screen in the app.
2. Full-bleed athlete photography with a bottom-up dark gradient overlay, carrying bottom-aligned uppercase headline copy and a full-width inverted (white-on-black) primary button.
3. A hexagonal (not circular, not star) achievement medal silhouette with a gradient fill, reserved exclusively for milestone celebrations.
4. A five-segment horizontal effort/zone bar showing time distribution across intensity bands.
5. A primary CTA that inverts the canvas — solid white pill with black uppercase text — as the dominant action color, saving the radioactive accent for in-progress/data moments.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas is true black on every single screen — never substitute a softer charcoal, and never default to a light theme (light mode may exist for accessibility only, never as the primary experience).
2. The radioactive accent must stay under roughly a fifth of any screen's surface area — it is a spotlight, not a color field; overusing it as a background exhausts the eye.
3. Every hero number and every button label renders in the heavy condensed display face, fully uppercase, with generous letter-spacing that widens as size shrinks — mixed case is reserved strictly for system-sans body and metadata text.
4. All numeric stats (pace, distance, elapsed time, heart rate) use monospaced/tabular digits so columns of results never jitter.
5. Reserve the heaviest haptic feedback tier for the two or three highest-commitment actions (starting a session, pausing) — never spend it on routine navigation like tab switches.
6. Achievement/milestone celebrations use a hexagonal medal shape exclusively — never a circle or star — so the pattern stays instantly recognizable as 'this is a Nike-style achievement.'
7. Cards and photography never carry a neutral drop shadow; on a black canvas, depth comes from the photo's own gradient overlay, not from Material-style elevation.
8. Split accent usage by verb: the radioactive accent belongs to in-progress/live moments (rings, active states), while the secondary intensity accent belongs strictly to post-session results and celebration — never mix the two roles.
9. The primary CTA inverts the canvas (solid light fill, dark uppercase text) rather than using the radioactive accent directly, so the accent stays reserved for data and progress.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / radioactive accent hex + secondary intensity accent hex:
- The core live-session screen: what 3 stats lead, and what the central ring measures:
- Achievement/milestone shape and tiering (what unlocks a medal, what tiers exist):
- Coach/guide persona (if any) and how their voice appears in copy and cards:
- Effort/zone system (if applicable) — how many bands, what they measure, what colors:
- Bottom navigation tabs (list 4-5):
- Haptic-intensity map: which 2-3 actions deserve the heaviest haptic tier:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version; note if a watch companion view is also needed):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Swift `Color` and `Font` token extension file matching the palette/type ladder above, adapted to the project's stated accent colors.
2. A SwiftUI live-session tracking screen: black canvas, 3-up stat row, and a large circular progress ring with a screaming hero number centered inside it.
3. A SwiftUI full-bleed hero card component (photography + gradient overlay + bottom-aligned uppercase headline + inverted primary CTA) for pre-session hype screens.
4. A SwiftUI hexagonal achievement medal component with a reveal animation (scale + fade + a small particle burst) gated to milestone events only.
5. A five-segment effort/zone bar component showing proportional time-in-zone.
6. A bottom tab bar implementation with the specified tabs, using an underline-dot active indicator rather than a tint pill.
7. A haptic and motion map: which interactions get which haptic tier, and which hero elements must stay fixed-size (not scaled by Dynamic Type) because the visual identity depends on them.

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in behavior-change and coaching apps — interfaces that need to feel like an encouraging human coach, not a clinical tracker, while still surfacing real data cleanly.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (light, default):
- Canvas #FBFBFD (soft near-white, never pure white), surface #FFFFFF, surface-subtle (chips/tracks) #F2F3F7, divider #E6E7EC
- Dark mode: canvas #121212, surface #1C1C1E, surface-subtle #262629, divider #2E2E31
- Primary action blue #2A5DF6 (pressed #1E47C8), progress/positive teal #1FC29B, deep anchor navy #0C1B4D
- A fixed, theme-invariant three-color classification system (never reordered, never reused elsewhere): green #34C759, yellow #FFC531, red #FF5A52 — each with a 16%-opacity tint variant for pill fills
- A distinct secondary-surface accent for a 'human coaching' feature, separate from the data-blue world: #7B61FF
- Text: primary #1A1A1F light / #F0F0F2 dark, secondary #6A6A70 / #9A9AA0

Typography: a rounded, geometric humanist sans throughout (friendly circular letterforms), used at 400 for prose and 700-800 for stats. Ladder: screen title 32/800, greeting/personal-header 26/700, hero stat 24/800, section title 22/700, card title 18/700, body 16/400, list-item name 15/600, meta line 14/400, uppercase tracked eyebrow 12/600, button label 16/700, small pill/category label 11/700, tab label 10/600.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit up to 40pt. Screen horizontal inset 18pt, card padding 16-18pt, vertical gap between cards 14-16pt. Radius scale: every button and pill uses a full/999pt radius (no sharp-cornered buttons anywhere), data cards use 16-18pt radius, the signature hero card uses 20pt, small inner chips 8-12pt.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A saturated diagonal-gradient hero card (two brand hues blending) that leads the daily feed — carrying an uppercase eyebrow, a punchy title, a thin progress bar, and an inverted (white-on-gradient) pill CTA. It should be the single most visually saturated element on the screen.
2. A fixed three-color classification dot/pill applied to every logged item, so users learn to 'read' entries by color at a glance rather than by number alone.
3. A thin, segmented horizontal bar showing the day's proportion across the three fixed categories, sitting above the entry list as an at-a-glance summary.
4. A trend/progress chart with a solid trend line in the primary action color and a dashed goal line in the secondary progress color.
5. A chat-style coaching surface using its own distinct accent color, visually separated from the rest of the data-driven blue interface.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The fixed three-color classification system (its exact hues) must never change between light and dark mode and must never be reused for any other purpose in the app — once a user learns to read by color, breaking that mapping breaks the core mechanic.
2. The daily/leading hero card is always the most saturated, most colorful element in the feed — never let a data card or chart out-compete it visually, and never place it below other content.
3. Every button, pill, chip, and search field uses a fully rounded (pill) shape — a sharp-cornered rectangular button is a visual inconsistency in this system, not a stylistic choice.
4. Keep prose and conversational copy at a light/regular weight even when adjacent to heavy numeric stats — the contrast between soft body text and bold numbers is what keeps the tone friendly rather than shouty.
5. Reserve a fully separate accent color for any human-coaching or chat surface, so it reads as a distinct 'people' space apart from the blue 'data' space.
6. Tint shadows and overlays toward the deep brand navy rather than neutral black — this keeps elevation feeling warm rather than harsh, especially in light mode.
7. Never use a stark pure-white or pure-black canvas — both light and dark canvases should sit one soft step in from those extremes.
8. Copy should read as encouraging and coach-like, never clinical — this is a tone rule that should inform placeholder text and empty states, not just marketing copy.
9. Tab-bar and segmented-control active states are conveyed by color/fill change alone — never add a Material-style background tint pill behind an active icon.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / primary action color + secondary progress color (hex):
- What the daily hero/lesson card should promote (a lesson, a challenge, a habit prompt) and its gradient colors:
- The fixed 3-category classification system this app needs (name each category, its meaning, and a proposed color):
- The core trend/progress metric shown on a graph, and what its goal line represents:
- Whether there's a human-coaching or chat feature, and its distinct accent color:
- Bottom navigation tabs (list 4-5):
- Tone/voice guidelines beyond 'encouraging' (any words or phrases to avoid):
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version; note if Android/Web variants are also needed):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Swift `Color` and `Font` token extension file for light and dark mode, matching the palette/type ladder above adapted to the project's brand colors.
2. A SwiftUI hero/lesson gradient card component with the eyebrow, title, thin progress bar, and inverted pill CTA, including its entrance animation.
3. A SwiftUI list-row component using the fixed 3-category classification dot + tinted category pill + trailing value.
4. A SwiftUI stacked segmented ratio bar showing proportional distribution across the 3 categories, with a re-animate-on-change transition.
5. A SwiftUI trend-graph card with a solid trend line, a dashed goal line, and a callout on tap.
6. A SwiftUI chat/coaching surface component (bubble styles for incoming vs outgoing, composer, distinct accent) if the project calls for one.
7. Accessibility notes: which elements should scale under Dynamic Type versus stay fixed, and VoiceOver phrasing for the classification system and the ratio bar.

whatYouGet: Full color and type spec for a dark, tri-domain biometric 'instrument panel' interface

content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in calm, precise biometric dashboards — interfaces that must feel like a cockpit instrument, dense with data but never noisy, where color always carries meaning rather than decoration.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles:
- Canvas: cool near-black #0B0B0F (never pure black), surface-1 (cards) #16161C, surface-2 (raised/sheets) #1E1E26, surface-3 (pressed/track) #27272F, divider #2A2A33
- A tri-domain color language where each of three tracked domains owns one hue used consistently everywhere it appears (ring, its contributing sub-metrics, its trend line): domain-A teal #4FD1C5, domain-B indigo #7C6FF0, domain-C amber #F5A623 — with a 'deep/pressed' variant of each for interactive states
- Text: primary white #FFFFFF, secondary #9A9AA5, tertiary #6A6A73
- Semantic deltas: positive reuses domain-A's teal, negative is a soft desaturated coral #E0746B (never a harsh red), neutral gray #9A9AA5

Typography: a clean geometric sans, weight band restricted to 400/600/700 only (no light, no black), tabular figures mandatory on every score/metric/delta. Ladder: hero ring score 52/700 tight tracking, screen title 26/700, section header 20/700, secondary/smaller ring score 34/700, card title 17/600, metric value 22/600, list-item name 15/600, body 15/400, small caption/unit 13/400, delta value 13/600, uppercase domain label 13/700 tracked +0.8, button 16/600, tab label 11/600.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit up to 56pt. Standard margin 16pt, section gap 24pt. Radius scale: 6pt small bar fills, 16pt cards/tiles, 20pt sheets/segmented controls, 24pt pill buttons, 18pt tag chips, circle for rings/avatars.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A circular 0-100 score gauge, rounded stroke cap, that sweeps clockwise and reveals with the arc animating in sync with a counting-up center number — used at multiple sizes (hero and small summary tile) across the whole app.
2. A vertical list breaking one score into its contributing sub-metrics, each row showing a name, a horizontal mini progress bar in that domain's color, and a value.
3. A detail screen that commits to exactly one domain's hue for its entire duration — no screen mixes two domain colors as primary accents.
4. Elevation conveyed purely through a surface-lightness ladder (three or four discrete steps) rather than shadows, with real shadows reserved only for sheets and one 'actively expanded' panel state.
5. A neutral (non-domain-colored) navigation chrome — the tab bar or top bar never adopts a domain's hue, keeping domain color strictly inside content.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. Color is information, not decoration: once a domain is assigned a hue, that hue must follow it everywhere — the ring, every contributing sub-metric, every trend line, every label — with zero exceptions.
2. Cap the palette at exactly the number of tracked domains plus neutrals; do not introduce a fourth 'accent' color that has no domain meaning.
3. Every score, metric value, and delta uses tabular/monospaced digits, since the counting-up reveal animation and any tabular list depend on digits not reflowing.
4. Any given detail or focused screen should commit to one domain's color as its sole accent for that screen — mixing two domain hues as co-primary accents on one screen defeats the color-as-meaning system.
5. Keep the canvas a cool near-black rather than pure black or true charcoal — this reads as 'night instrument' rather than either 'off' or 'flat gray.'
6. Depth comes from a surface-value ladder (canvas → card → raised → sheet), not from drop shadows, except for sheets and one genuinely-expanded/focused panel state which may get a soft diffuse shadow.
7. Use a soft desaturated tone (never a harsh alert red) for 'declining/negative' deltas — the visual vocabulary should stay calm even when reporting a downward trend.
8. Keep all navigation chrome (tab bar, top bar) neutral/monochrome — domain color must never leak into chrome, or it stops signaling 'this specific metric' and starts just meaning 'decoration.'
9. The score-reveal animation (arc sweep + counting number) should ease out so it decelerates into its final value, never a linear tick — this is what makes the reveal feel considered rather than mechanical.
</house_rules>

name: Peloton Design System
summary: Recreate Peloton's studio-black UI — cinematic class cards, output ring, and live leaderboard — as a SwiftUI prompt.
description: A deep-extraction prompt for Peloton's pure-black canvas, single red accent, and in-class metrics/leaderboard components, for generating an on-brand live-fitness-class interface.

whatYouGet: Full color and type spec for a pure-black, single-red-accent boutique-studio interface
Component specs for the cinematic class card, in-class output ring, and real-time leaderboard
House rules protecting the one-brand-color discipline and the fixed in-class metric color-coding
content.promptText:
<role>
You are a senior iOS product designer and SwiftUI engineer who specializes in premium live-fitness-class experiences — interfaces that need to feel like a dim, cinematic studio on a phone screen, where one disciplined brand color and real photography do all the emotional work.
</role>

<reference_data>
Color roles (the only mode — no light theme):
- Canvas: pure black #000000 (never a softer charcoal substitute), surface-1 (cards) #121212, surface-2 (pills/inputs) #1C1C1E, surface-3 (tracks) #262629, divider #2C2C2E
- The single brand color: #DF1E2E for solid fills, brightened to #FF4B57 for text/active glyphs on black (contrast-corrected), pressed state #B81825
- A 'selected = solid light fill, dark text' inverted chip pattern using pure white
- Text: primary #FFFFFF, secondary #B5B5BA, tertiary #7A7A80
- Fixed in-class metric colors (never recolor, color IS the data): metric-1 (power/output) brand red, metric-2 (cadence) #E5402A, metric-3 (resistance/incline) #F0A030, metric-4 (heart rate) brightened brand red, a distinct blue #3DB8E0 for a composite/zone score, and a green #2ECC71 reserved for personal-record celebrations

Typography: a single confident sans throughout, set very heavy (800-900 weight) with tight/negative tracking on titles and hero numbers, tabular figures mandatory on anything that ticks live. Ladder: in-session hero metric 44/900 tight, screen title 32/900, hero/detail title 26/800, section header 22/800, card title 17/800, live metric value 18/800 tabular, leaderboard value 14/800 tabular, body 15/600, meta line 14/400, uppercase eyebrow (in the brand's brightened accent) 12/700 tracked, uppercase small label 11/600 tracked, button 15/700, tab label 10/600, badge 10/800 uppercase.

Spacing/radius: 4pt base unit up to 48pt. Card padding ~14x16pt, card-to-card gap 18pt, screen inset 16pt. Radius scale: 5pt small status badges, 14pt cards, 20pt sheets, full pill for every button/filter chip/search field, circle for rings and avatars.

Distinctive patterns to reproduce:
1. A cinematic, full-bleed thumbnail card with a baked-in bottom gradient scrim for text legibility, a pulsing 'live now' badge in the top corner, and an uppercase category eyebrow in the brand's brightened accent above a heavy title.
2. A horizontally scrolling filter-pill row where the selected pill inverts to a solid light fill with dark text (rather than tinting to the brand color).
3. A live-session metrics screen anchored by a thick circular output ring (brand-colored arc on a dark track) with a huge tabular number at its center, alongside a column of fixed-color live metric rows.
4. A real-time ranked list where every participant's row reorders live as values change, with the viewer's own row given a translucent brand-color background wash.
5. Depth conveyed by surface-lightness steps and photography gradients rather than shadows, since shadows are nearly invisible on a pure-black canvas.
</reference_data>

<house_rules>
1. The canvas is pure black on every screen, always — there is no light mode, and no charcoal substitute; this is a dark-studio brand by design, not merely a dark-mode option.
2. There is exactly one brand color; it appears as a solid fill for badges/CTAs/rings and as a brightened, contrast-corrected variant for text and active glyphs on the black canvas — never introduce a second brand hue.
3. Fixed in-class metric colors are locked semantics — the same metric always renders in the same color regardless of theme, because the color itself carries meaning (a user should recognize 'that's my heart rate row' by hue alone).
4. Selected/active pills, chips, and segmented controls invert to a solid light (white) fill with dark text — this is the signature 'selected' pattern and should not be replaced with a brand-color tint.
5. All live-ticking numerals (leaderboard, in-session metrics, timers) use tabular/monospaced digits so ranked lists and metric columns never visually jitter as values update.
6. Never drop-shadow flat content cards — depth on a black canvas comes from a lighter surface step and, for photography, a baked gradient scrim; reserve real shadows for genuinely floating sheets/dialogs only.
7. A personal-record or milestone moment gets a distinct, separate celebratory color (not the primary brand color) plus a brief animation and haptic — so it's recognizably different from the ordinary 'live/brand' signal.
8. The one small pulsing element in the whole system (a 'live now' indicator dot) is the closest thing to an idle animation — keep everything else quiet and purposeful so that pulse still reads as special.
9. Titles and hero numbers are always set heavy (extra-bold or heavier) with tight or negative letter-spacing — a light or loosely-tracked headline would undercut the confident, energetic tone.
</house_rules>

<the_project>
- App name / brand accent hex (fill + brightened text variant):
- What a 'class' or session card needs to show (category, instructor/host, duration, rating, live status):
- The in-class live metrics to track (name 3-5) and a fixed color for each:
- Whether there's a real-time ranked/leaderboard feature and what it ranks by:
- What counts as a celebratory milestone (PR, streak, goal) and its distinct celebration color:
- Bottom navigation tabs (list 4):
- Filter/category taxonomy for the main content browse screen:
- Platform target (iOS SwiftUI version; note if a video/streaming surface needs its own layout):
</the_project>

<what_to_give_me>
1. A complete Swift `Color` and `Font` token extension file matching the palette/type ladder above, adapted to the project's brand accent.
2. A SwiftUI cinematic content card component: thumbnail area, pulsing 'live' badge, uppercase category eyebrow, heavy title, host/instructor line, and meta row.
3. A SwiftUI filter-pill row component with the inverted-white 'selected' pattern and horizontal scroll.
4. A SwiftUI live-session metrics screen: a circular output ring with a centered tabular hero number, plus a column of fixed-color live metric rows.
5. A SwiftUI real-time ranked leaderboard component with reordering animation and a highlighted 'you' row.
6. A SwiftUI personal-record/milestone celebration component (distinct color, brief animation, haptic trigger).
7. A bottom tab bar implementation with the specified tabs, using a plain white active-state (no tint pill) to match the system's chrome discipline.
</what_to_give_me>
